meaning.en: Utterly shocked, as if struck on the head by thunder.
meaning.zh: 像被雷劈中头顶，形容受到巨大的打击或惊吓。

equivalents: hit like a ton of bricks

examples.zh: 听到噩耗，她如五雷轰顶，呆立在原地。
examples.en: On hearing the terrible news she stood rooted to the spot, thunderstruck.

examples.zh: 这个结果对他简直是五雷轰顶。
examples.en: The result hit him like a thunderbolt.

examples.zh: 得知公司破产，大家都有如五雷轰顶。
examples.en: Learning the company was bankrupt, everyone was stunned.

usage.en: Usually 如/有如五雷轰顶; also used in oaths (若有此事，五雷轰顶).
usage.zh: 常说“如五雷轰顶”；也用于发誓诅咒。

meaning.en: Smiling broadly, often too eagerly.
meaning.zh: 脸上布满笑容，多带有讨好的意味。

examples.zh: 店员满脸堆笑地迎上来。
examples.en: The shop assistant came over, all smiles.

examples.zh: 他满脸堆笑，向客户连连道歉。
examples.en: With a fixed smile he apologised to the client again and again.

examples.zh: 一见领导，他就满脸堆笑。
examples.en: The moment he saw the boss he was all smiles.

usage.en: Predicate or adverbial; often implies flattery.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、状语，常含讨好意味。

meaning.en: In a very short time.

equivalents: in the blink of an eye

examples.zh: 暴雨来了，顷刻之间街上就积满了水。
examples.en: The downpour came and in an instant the street was flooded.

examples.zh: 顷刻之间，一切都变了。
examples.en: In a moment, everything changed.

examples.zh: 大楼在顷刻之间倒塌。
examples.en: The building collapsed in a flash.

usage.en: Adverbial, usually sentence-initial.
usage.zh: 多作状语，常放句首。

meaning.en: Brimming with passion and idealism.

examples.zh: 年轻人满腔热血，渴望报效祖国。
examples.en: The young are full of fervour and eager to serve their country.

examples.zh: 他怀着满腔热血投身公益事业。
examples.en: He threw himself into charity work with burning passion.

examples.zh: 别用冷水浇灭他的满腔热血。
examples.en: Don't douse his passion with cold water.

usage.en: Attributive or object; carries idealistic tone.
usage.zh: 多作定语、宾语，带理想主义色彩。

meaning.en: Having no place to settle or stand one's ground.
meaning.zh: 没有容身、站稳脚跟的地方。

examples.zh: 房租涨得太快，穷人几乎无立足之地。
examples.en: Rents rose so fast that the poor had almost nowhere to stand.

examples.zh: 这种歪理邪说在学界无立足之地。
examples.en: Such fallacies have no foothold in academia.

examples.zh: 他被排挤得在公司无立足之地。
examples.en: Pushed out, he had no place left in the company.

usage.en: Predicate or object; literal and figurative.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、宾语，可指实际处所，也可比喻。

meaning.en: A wish that one may always be cheerful.
meaning.zh: 嘴巴常常张开笑着，祝愿人经常开心快乐。

examples.zh: 祝您身体健康，笑口常开！
examples.en: Wishing you good health and a smile always!

examples.zh: 乐观的人总是笑口常开。
examples.en: Optimistic people always have a smile.

examples.zh: 新年到，愿你笑口常开，万事如意。
examples.en: The New Year is here; may you smile often and have all you wish.

usage.en: Greeting or description; often with 祝/愿.
usage.zh: 用作祝福语或描写，常与“祝”“愿”连用。

meaning.en: To make mistakes when rushed.

examples.zh: 忙中出错，他把文件发给了别人。
examples.en: In the rush he sent the file to the wrong person.

examples.zh: 越是着急越要细心，免得忙中出错。
examples.en: The more urgent it is, the more careful you must be, to avoid errors.

examples.zh: 年底忙中出错的情况特别多。
examples.en: Slip-ups under pressure are especially common at year end.

usage.en: Predicate; often with 免得/小心.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与“免得”“小心”连用。

meaning.en: To go through a lot of trouble and many twists to get something done.

equivalents: go through a lot of trouble

examples.zh: 为了办这张证件，我大费周折。
examples.en: I went to great trouble to get this certificate.

examples.zh: 找到那家老店，他们大费周折。
examples.en: They went to considerable trouble to find that old shop.

examples.zh: 不必大费周折，打个电话就行。
examples.en: No need for all that bother; a phone call will do.

usage.en: Predicate; often with 不必/为了.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与“不必”“为了”连用。

meaning.en: Both parties are willing.

examples.zh: 婚姻要两厢情愿，不能强迫。
examples.en: Marriage must be by mutual consent, never forced.

examples.zh: 这桩买卖两厢情愿，谁也不吃亏。
examples.en: Both sides were willing, so nobody lost out.

examples.zh: 合作应当建立在两厢情愿的基础上。
examples.en: Cooperation should rest on mutual willingness.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; the opposite is 一厢情愿.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语；反义为“一厢情愿”。

synonyms: 周瑜打黄盖——一个愿打，一个愿挨

meaning.en: To have achieved outstanding things.

examples.zh: 他是一位在物理学领域卓有成就的科学家。
examples.en: He is a scientist of distinction in physics.

examples.zh: 这位作家卓有成就，作品被译成多国文字。
examples.en: The writer is highly accomplished, with works translated into many languages.

examples.zh: 几十年来他在教育界卓有成就。
examples.en: For decades he has achieved great things in education.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; stresses the achievements themselves, while 卓有成效 stresses effectiveness.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语；侧重成就，“卓有成效”侧重效果。

natural: the glow of the setting sun

meaning.en: The afterglow of the setting sun.
meaning.zh: 太阳落山后留下的光辉。

examples.zh: 湖面披上了落日余晖。
examples.en: The lake was cloaked in the glow of sunset.

examples.zh: 我们沐浴着落日余晖慢慢往回走。
examples.en: We walked slowly back, bathed in the sunset glow.

examples.zh: 老人坐在门前，望着落日余晖出神。
examples.en: The old man sat at the door, lost in the afterglow.

usage.en: Object or subject in descriptive prose; also a metaphor for old age.
usage.zh: 多作宾语、主语，用于写景，也可喻晚年。

meaning.en: Walking or moving with a swaying, unsteady gait.
meaning.zh: 身体左右摇晃、走路不稳的样子。

examples.zh: 小鸭子摇摇摆摆地走过来。
examples.en: The duckling waddled over.

examples.zh: 他喝多了，摇摇摆摆地回了家。
examples.en: He'd had too much and staggered home.

examples.zh: 宝宝摇摇摆摆地学走路。
examples.en: The baby wobbled along, learning to walk.

usage.en: Adverbial or predicate; cute or comic tone.
usage.zh: 多作状语、谓语，带可爱或滑稽色彩。

meaning.en: Intelligent and good at getting things done.

examples.zh: 她聪明能干，很快就当上了经理。
examples.en: Clever and capable, she soon became manager.

examples.zh: 大家都夸这孩子聪明能干。
examples.en: Everyone praises the child as bright and capable.

examples.zh: 我们要找一位聪明能干的助手。
examples.en: We need a clever and capable assistant.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语。

meaning.en: Not striving to improve oneself.

examples.zh: 他安于现状，不求上进。
examples.en: Content with how things are, he has no wish to improve.

examples.zh: 老师批评他学习上不求上进。
examples.en: The teacher criticised him for not striving in his studies.

examples.zh: 不求上进的人很难有大的成就。
examples.en: Those who don't strive seldom achieve much.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; critical tone.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，含批评。

meaning.en: To avoid unnecessary losses and keep one's strength for later.
meaning.zh: 避免损耗，留着力量以备后用。

examples.zh: 主力球员轮休，保存实力迎接决赛。
examples.en: The key players rested to save their strength for the final.

examples.zh: 公司选择收缩业务，保存实力。
examples.en: The company scaled back to conserve its strength.

examples.zh: 他在小组赛中有意保存实力。
examples.en: He deliberately held something back in the group stage.

usage.en: Predicate; strategic, sometimes slightly evasive.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，带策略意味，有时略含回避。

meaning.en: To be held back by concerns or scruples.
meaning.zh: 因担心而有所顾虑，不敢放开去做。

examples.zh: 碍于面子，他说话有所顾忌。
examples.en: For the sake of face, he was guarded in what he said.

examples.zh: 既然有所顾忌，就不必勉强。
examples.en: If you have misgivings, don't force yourself.

examples.zh: 领导在场，大家发言都有所顾忌。
examples.en: With the boss present, everyone was cautious in speaking.

usage.en: Predicate; its opposite is 无所顾忌.
usage.zh: 多作谓语；反义为“无所顾忌”。

meaning.en: Clumsy and awkward in movement.

examples.zh: 我笨手笨脚的，别把杯子打碎了。
examples.en: I'm clumsy; I hope I don't break the cup.

examples.zh: 新来的学徒笨手笨脚，常常出错。
examples.en: The new apprentice is all thumbs and often makes mistakes.

examples.zh: 他笨手笨脚地系着领带。
examples.en: He fumbled with his tie.

usage.en: Predicate or adverbial; self-deprecating or critical.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、状语，可自嘲或批评。

meaning.en: Young and not yet knowing better.

examples.zh: 他当时年幼无知，才做了这件错事。
examples.en: He was too young to know better when he did this wrong.

examples.zh: 请原谅孩子年幼无知。
examples.en: Please forgive the child, who is too young to understand.

examples.zh: 年幼无知的孩子容易受骗。
examples.en: Young, naive children are easy to deceive.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; often used as an excuse.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，常用于为人开脱。

meaning.en: To die, especially unexpectedly.
meaning.zh: 丧失性命，多指意外死去。

examples.zh: 他酒后驾车，不幸命丧黄泉。
examples.en: He drove drunk and unfortunately lost his life.

examples.zh: 多少英雄命丧黄泉，无人知晓。
examples.en: How many heroes met their end, unknown to anyone.

examples.zh: 一场大火让数人命丧黄泉。
examples.en: A fire cost several people their lives.

usage.en: Predicate; written and news style.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面、新闻语体。

meaning.en: Impossible to put into words.

examples.zh: 看到故乡的变化，他心中有一种难以名状的感觉。
examples.en: Seeing his hometown changed, he felt something indescribable.

examples.zh: 她的喜悦难以名状。
examples.en: Her joy was beyond words.

examples.zh: 这种难以名状的恐惧一直缠着他。
examples.en: This nameless fear kept haunting him.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; for feelings and scenes.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，形容心情或景象。

meaning.en: To turn an enemy into a friend.

examples.zh: 她以宽容化敌为友。
examples.en: Through generosity she turned an enemy into a friend.

examples.zh: 谈判让两家公司化敌为友。
examples.en: The negotiations turned the two firms from rivals into friends.

examples.zh: 真诚是化敌为友的最好办法。
examples.en: Sincerity is the best way to turn foes into friends.

usage.en: Predicate; often with 能/学会.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与“能”“学会”连用。

meaning.en: A very heavy responsibility.

examples.zh: 家里的千斤重担压在他一个人肩上。
examples.en: The heavy burden of the family rested on his shoulders alone.

examples.zh: 新校长肩负着千斤重担。
examples.en: The new principal shoulders a huge responsibility.

examples.zh: 大家一起分担，千斤重担也能变轻。
examples.en: Shared among everyone, even a heavy burden gets lighter.

usage.en: Object; usually 肩负/挑起千斤重担.
usage.zh: 多作宾语，常说“肩负/挑起千斤重担”。
